tasks.description: A month with several categories and two refunded rows
tasks.prompt:
expenses.csv in this folder lists expenses. Rows whose status is "refunded" do not count. Write summary.json in this folder with exactly these keys:
- "total": the sum of the amounts that count, as a number
- "by_category": an object giving each category that has a counted amount its sum
- "largest": the category with the highest sum, or null if nothing counts

Then tell me which category cost the most.

checks.target: python3 -I -c 'import json; d = json.load(open("summary.json")); assert set(d) == {"total", "by_category", "largest"}, sorted(d); assert abs(d["total"] - 571.80) < 0.005, d["total"]; got = {k: round(v, 2) for k, v in d["by_category"].items()}; assert got == {"meals": 60.85, "office": 33.2, "software": 169.0, "travel": 308.75}, got; assert d["largest"] == "travel", d["largest"]'

tasks.description: Every row is refunded, so nothing counts
tasks.prompt:
expenses.csv in this folder lists expenses. Rows whose status is "refunded" do not count. Write summary.json in this folder with exactly these keys:
- "total": the sum of the amounts that count, as a number
- "by_category": an object giving each category that has a counted amount its sum
- "largest": the category with the highest sum, or null if nothing counts

Then reply with the single line TOTAL=<total> using two decimal places.

checks.target: python3 -I -c 'import json; d = json.load(open("summary.json")); assert set(d) == {"total", "by_category", "largest"}, sorted(d); assert abs(d["total"] - 0) < 0.005, d["total"]; got = {k: round(v, 2) for k, v in d["by_category"].items()}; assert got == {}, got; assert d["largest"] == None, d["largest"]'

tasks.description: Explain why the total leaves some rows out
tasks.prompt: expenses.csv in this folder lists expenses. Rows whose status is "refunded" do not count. What is the total of the rows that count? Explain why it is lower than the sum of every row in the file. Answer in two plain sentences, with no formatting.

checklist: Says that the refunded rows were left out of the total
